recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants a current enforceable style policy for all HL7 V2/v3/SNOMED CT/LOINC references, file a new editorial tracker with the exact convention and scope rather than using this already-applied DSTU1 issue as authority for bulk edits.
issue_request: FHIR-8660 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core request to standardize references to other HL7 messaging standards and terminology systems in documentation, including v2/V2/v3/V3, SNOMED CT, and LOINC spelling.
initial_application: SVN revision 6893, imported as git commit 0cabf5ff9d9ed05d5b518b82901fc8d2698e0f65, explicitly mentions #8660 and performed a broad non-substantive wording sweep across comparison pages, resource notes, terminology pages, spreadsheets, and tooling files.
additional_context: Current source still contains multiple naming forms, but the remaining differences are broad editorial/product-label choices rather than a forgotten conformance rule. The 2023 QA commit dad7cf37c75822c352509e1c2e8d050408d0be18 intentionally changed comparison-v2.html from HL7 v2 to HL7 V2, while v3, SNOMED CT, and LOINC are represented with current capitalization in active source. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later final decision requiring a new global rewrite.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reapplying the 2015 lowercase-v convention or attempting a fresh repository-wide style sweep would be broad non-semantic churn and could conflict with later source choices; it is not necessary to make the current specification correct.

evidence_items.summary: Current source contains the present HL7 V2/v3, SNOMED CT, LOINC, and v2 mapping naming surface in active source pages and metadata.
evidence_items.learned: Any remaining variation is broad editorial terminology rather than a discrete conformance or semantic error needing a surgical fix.
